main_body: A wooden rack base box (rows ~25-47) holding three upright spears; the base is drawn as stacked front-facing shelf compartments with a thin top edge.
top_band: Dark brown outline at rows 25-26, then an orange/tan strip at rows 27-28 that reads as a front-facing shelf band; no distinct lighter horizontal top surface at least 3 rows tall.
evidence: Down the middle column of the base: dark outline (25-26), a 2-row orange band (27-28), then red-brown front face and dark dividers, shelf gaps (32-37), and a second crate-like front with a notched top edge (38-40) and an orange band (41-42). Every band is a vertical front-facing panel or a thin rim; no horizontal top or shelf surface is visible from above. The spears are plain vertical poles. The base has no top face and the rack beams show no top surfaces, so this is a front elevation.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark brown tint beside the wood, which fits the standard. The spear shafts are flat orange-brown with only 2-3 tones, and the spearheads are small and pale. The base has a few highlight bands and some notch detail, but its panels are largely flat fills. Tiles carry fewer colours and less grain than the stall and well references, which have 5-6 steps and rich texture.
